claims.text: The initial nanoparticles are equimolar, single-phase CoCrFeMnNi solid solutions.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles have minimal lattice strain.
The initial nanoparticles exhibit only slight short-range ordering.
Adding less than 5 at.% of a size-mismatched dopant such as Au or Cu will systematically increase or tune local lattice strain in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Enhanced local lattice strain disrupts atomic diffusion pathways.
Dopant-induced lattice strain raises the activation energy for atomic diffusion.
Slower atomic diffusion kinetically suppresses nanoscale clustering, phase separation, and elemental segregation.
Less than 5 at.% dopant will allow the alloy to retain sufficient overall equimolarity for the proposed stabilization mechanism.
Doped CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will remain more chemically uniform and more nearly single-phase than undoped nanoparticles during identical thermal cycling.
Doped nanoparticles will undergo smaller changes in short-range order than undoped nanoparticles.
Undoped CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will show detectable clustering or phase demixing near the upper end of the 473–1923 K range.
The proposed stability advantage will persist across thermal cycling from 473 K to 1923 K.
The stabilizing effect is significant only below 5 at.% dopant.
An inert atmosphere is required because oxidation could otherwise dominate nanoparticle surface chemistry.
The controlled comparison is between doped and undoped CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles subjected to identical inert-atmosphere thermal cycling from 473 K to 1923 K.
The hypothesis is falsified if doped nanoparticles show diffusion rates, clustering, or phase separation similar to or greater than those of the undoped control under the same thermal conditions.
